transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this review to work through the disposition of the 480 castings from Cell 7 currently on quality hold. As you know, we had an abnormal cooling event during yesterday's run, and I need to make a final disposition decision before these parts can be released to machining. Before I decide, I'd like to hear from each of you on your respective areas. Let's start with metrology -- have we completed any dimensional or non-destructive testing beyond the initial visual inspection? And maintenance, what's the status on the cooling system repair? I also need production control's input on scheduling impact. Let's work through this systematically.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Elena. Yes, I've completed a dimensional review of all 480 castings. 312 of them meet the flatness limit of 0.30 mm or less, but 168 measure above 0.30 mm and will need to be reworked before they can be released. I finished the measurement report this morning, but it's still in the metrology report queue and hasn't reached you yet.

transcript.text: Good morning, Elena. On the maintenance side, I inspected Cell 7's cooling system this morning and found that the cooling-fan belt is damaged and must be replaced before we can run another production cycle. I confirmed with my maintenance technician that the replacement will take exactly 2 hours. I should note that the work order hasn't been entered into the system yet, but I wanted to bring this to the group now so it's factored into the disposition and scheduling discussion.
